problemText: Evaluate: |-15|
hints: The two straight bars ask one question: how far is this number from zero?
Distance is never negative. Count the units from -15 back to zero.

problemText: Evaluate: -|-6|
hints: The bars act like parentheses: finish what is inside them before you touch anything outside.
Inside the bars you get 6. There is still a minus sign in front, waiting its turn.

problemText: How far apart are -9 and 4 on the number line? Type your answer as a number.
hints: The distance between two numbers is the absolute value of their difference: |-9 - 4|.
You can also count the jumps: nine steps from -9 up to 0, then keep counting to 4.

problemText: Which of these has the greatest value?
hints: Work each one out to a single number first, then compare those numbers.
A minus sign sitting OUTSIDE the bars does not disappear, so -|-20| is not 20.

problemText: Evaluate: |-4| - |-9|
hints: Clear each set of bars first, then do the subtraction that is left.
The bars turn this into 4 - 9. Taking 9 away from 4 crosses zero.

problemText: In a card game Ravi's score is -12 points and Nora's score is 8 points. Whose score is further from zero, and by how much further?
hints: How far a score sits from zero is its absolute value, no matter which side of zero it is on.
Find |-12| and |8|, then subtract the smaller distance from the larger one to see how much further.

problemText: Which of these numbers sits between -3 and -2 on the number line?
hints: Start at zero and walk left. Count the WHOLE units you pass before the decimal part even starts.
A number between -2 and -3 is more than 2 units from zero but less than 3 units from zero.

problemText: Which decimal lands on exactly the same point of the number line as -3/4?
hints: The fraction bar means divide. Which number goes inside the division box, the 3 or the 4?
Work out 3 divided by 4, not 4 divided by 3, and keep the number on the left side of zero.

problemText: Write 7/4 as a decimal. Type your answer as a decimal number.
hints: A fraction bar is a division sign, so this is 7 divided by 4. Put the 7 inside.
7 is bigger than 4, so the answer is more than 1 whole. Write 7 as 7.00 and divide until the remainder is zero.

problemText: Ana says -7 is not a rational number, because it is not written as a fraction. Which response is correct?
choices: She is right: a number must already be written as a fraction to be rational.
She is right: -7 has no denominator, so no fraction can equal it.
She is wrong: -7 can be written as -7/1, so it is rational.
She is right: negative numbers are never rational.
hints: Go back to the definition: a rational number is any number you CAN write as one integer over another.
Ask yourself what happens if you put a 1 underneath -7. Does that change its value?

problemText: Each unit on a number line is cut into 4 equal parts. Starting at 0 and counting 5 parts to the LEFT, which number do you land on?
hints: Counting 5 parts when each unit holds 4 of them means you go past the first whole unit.
Four parts carry you all the way to -1. The fifth part keeps going left, a quarter of a unit further.

problemText: Point P sits exactly halfway between -1.25 and -0.75 on the number line. What number is P?
hints: Halfway between two numbers means their sum divided by 2 - or count the gap and step half of it.
The gap from -1.25 to -0.75 is 0.5 units wide, so P sits 0.25 to the RIGHT of -1.25.

problemText: Which of these numbers is the greatest: -12, -8, -20, -3 ?
hints: Put all four on a number line. Greatest always means furthest RIGHT.
Every one of these is negative, so the one closest to zero is the one furthest right.

problemText: Which statement is true?
hints: Line up the decimal places first: compare the sizes 3.50 and 3.05, and remember a positive always beats a negative.
Both numbers are negative, so the bigger SIZE sits further left - and further left is smaller.

problemText: Of the numbers -2.5, -2.05 and -2.55, which one is the LEAST? Type it as a number.
hints: Line up the decimal places first: compare the sizes 2.50, 2.05 and 2.55.
All three are negative, so the one with the LARGEST size sits furthest left, and furthest left is least.

problemText: Which of these numbers is the greatest: 2/3, 5/8, 0.63, -0.95 ?
hints: Drop anything negative straight away, then turn each fraction into a decimal by dividing top by bottom.
2 divided by 3 is 0.666..., and 5 divided by 8 is 0.625. Write all three as 0.666, 0.625 and 0.630 before you decide - you cannot compare fractions by their top numbers alone.

problemText: Which list is in order from LEAST to GREATEST?
hints: Turn every number into a decimal first, then sort the negatives, zero and positives as three groups.
-3/4 is -0.75 and 3/5 is 0.6. Among the negatives, the larger size sits further left, so it comes first.

problemText: A number n is greater than -1/2 and less than -0.2. Which of these could be n?
hints: Write -1/2 as a decimal so both fences are in the same form, then picture the stretch of line between them.
n has to sit to the RIGHT of -0.5 and to the LEFT of -0.2, so its distance from zero is between 0.2 and 0.5.

problemText: Write 6% as a decimal.
hints: Percent means out of 100, so start by writing 6% as the fraction 6/100.
Leaving a percent makes the number smaller, so the point slides two places LEFT. Start from 6.0 and slide it twice.

problemText: Which of these is equal to 1/3?
hints: The fraction bar means divide, so this is 1 divided by 3 - not the digits 1 and 3 written around a point.
Write 1 as 1.000 and divide. The remainder 1 keeps coming back, so the same digit repeats forever.

problemText: Write 3/8 as a percent. Type just the number, without the percent sign.
hints: Divide 3 by 8 first. Write the 3 as 3.000 and keep going until the remainder is zero.
3 divided by 8 is 0.375. Now multiply by 100, which slides the point two places to the RIGHT.

problemText: Write 35% as a fraction in simplest form.
hints: Percent means out of one hundred, so write the number over 100 first.
Both 35 and 100 divide by 5. Do not stop before you have simplified.

problemText: Which of these is the greatest: 0.7, 68%, 3/4, 5/8 ?
hints: Put all four into the same form. Decimals are easiest: divide each fraction top by bottom, and slide the percent two places LEFT.
68% is 0.68 and 5/8 is 0.625. Now line up 0.700, 0.680 and 0.625 against the decimal for 3/4.

problemText: A video game has 20 levels. Leo has finished 65% of them. How many levels does he have LEFT to finish?
hints: Turn 65% into a decimal first, then use it to find how many of the 20 levels Leo has already finished.
65% is 0.65, and 0.65 x 20 = 13 levels finished. The question asks for the ones still left out of 20.
